risk_flags.note: Corpus lacks detailed quantitative evidence such as recent form, injury status, exact head-to-head, and court-speed specifics.
Players are deliberately masked as Player S and Player R; initialization preserves masking and avoids identity inference.
Best-of-three finals can swing on a few points, limiting confidence in broad priors.
Forecast resolves strictly on title outcome; near-miss or strong performance without title still resolves no.

simulation_brief.resolution_rule: yes only if Player S wins the women's singles title; runner_up_or_loss_resolves_no
simulation_brief.summary: Player S, world No. 1 and experienced Australian Open finalist, faces Player R, a fifth seed with a powerful serve and prior major-title experience, in the women's singles final. Player S has ranking and recent Melbourne-final experience advantages, but the match is competitive and best-of-three variance is material.
uncertainty_notes: Source corpus is sparse and intentionally masked.
No detailed injury, surface-speed, draw-fatigue, or exact head-to-head data provided.
Outcome is unresolved at T0; runner-up status would resolve the forecast as no.
